title: The torsion diagonal classes as one morphism of inverse systems
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $Y$. Put $W=\mathbf P^1_Y\times_Y\mathbf P^1_Y$ and let
$\Delta:\mathbf P^1_Y\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal, and write $\Delta_*$ for the direct image on pro-etale sheaves from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. After pullback to the pro-etale site, $\mathbf G_m$ denotes $\nu_W^*\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$, where $\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$ is the etale sheaf of units from [sk-def-kummer], and $\nu_W^*$ is the exact inverse image under the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use the small site and coefficient-category conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write
$D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$ for the derived category of inverse systems
$(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ [def-weil-inverse-system] of sheaves of $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules on
$W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. The pro-étale pullback of the Cartier extension
   $0\to\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to0$ of the diagonal
   (with $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$ for a local equation $t$ of $\Delta$) defines a
   morphism $\partial:\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to\mathbf G_m[1]$ in
   $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf Z)$, represented by the roof
   $\Delta_*\mathbf Z\xleftarrow{\sim}[\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta]\to\mathbf G_m[1]$
   with the two-term complex in degrees $-1,0$.
2. The functor
   $T:K\mapsto K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}(\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n})_{n\geq1}$
   (the left derived change of rings of the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]) is a well-defined exact functor
   $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf Z)\to D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$, and
   $R\varprojlim\circ T$ is derived $\ell$-completion.
3. There are isomorphisms of systems
   $T(\Delta_*\mathbf Z)\simeq\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet$ and
   $T(\mathbf G_m[1])\simeq\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$, where the transition
   maps of $\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)=(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, sk-def-sp-tate-twist] are
   $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$.
4. Under these identifications $c_\bullet=T(\partial)$ is a morphism
   $\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet\to\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$ in
   $D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$ whose $n$-th level is the torsion cycle
   class of $\Delta$ with coefficients $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ of
   [sk-lem-geo-cartier].

proof.text: Construct both simultaneous strict cokernel reductions using exists_diagonalDerivedReduction, including its computation on complexes whose prime-power scalar maps are monic. The explicit additive cokernel functor and its quotient transitions supply the strict system.

Multiplication by a nonzero integer is monic on the specified lifted integer constant. Constant sheafification preserves this and lowerStar preserves monomorphisms. Consequently the degree-zero complex of the supported integral constant belongs to the computation class, so its derived single counit is an isomorphism.
Apply diagonal_reduction_completion to the constructed p-adic reduction; it supplies the two total derived limits, the scalar comparison and the integral orthogonal reflection unit.

With a the isomorphism of the actual source counit, apply diagonal_kummer_reduction for the normalized strict Kummer target and full finite Cartier class. The cycle predicate packages these normalized data, and the inverse Ext/Hom equivalence recovers the unique system class.

proof_origin.place: Strict derived reduction, supported source counit and combination of completion and normalized Kummer components.

lean.note: Strict inverse systems of modules over the constant Z_l sheaf, presented by fixed-scalar module-valued sheaves. Ordinary reduction is fixed by cokernel universal properties and quotient transitions; its everywhere-defined left derived pair retains the actual strict system category. Comparison units, the positive roof sign, integral derived completion, and the full normalized finite Cartier arrows are explicit. Repair R2: additionally asserts intrinsic derived ell-completeness (right orthogonality to ell-invertible complexes) and a natural completion unit with its universal Hom property. Repair R1: the published Cartier definitions are attributed to def-sfb-cartier-reduction-data, rather than citing the unused comparison theorem. Repair F1/R4 (consumer specialization; no dependency-record repair): def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category retains NH's ringedSiteModules and its owning file. DiagonalMod uses Mathlib Sheaf J (ModuleCat (ULift Z_l)), the fixed-scalar presentation of modules over the constant ring sheaf: constant scalar actions extend uniquely by local gluing, and conversely the ring-sheaf action restricts to constant sections; these inverse presentations have the same linear morphisms, sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels. def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product retains Q46's CochainTensorUniverses record: diagonalScalarExtension implements the same balanced tensor by ModuleCat.extendScalars and sheafification, with its insertion-of-one adjunction; DiagonalReductionPresentation specifies tensor with the finite quotient by cokernels and quotient transitions. sk-def-sp-tate-twist retains N4's ProEtaleTateTwistsOfUniverses record: the finite first twist used here is the actual proEtaleRootsOfUnityTower with power-ell transitions and geoCartierLine at each finite residue ring, with cartierProRootMap fixing its tensor generator and scalar action. The nonfinite condensed-coefficient construction is not substituted for the discrete constant Z_l tower. All three dependency files are restored byte-identically to newtargets-dag, preserving their owning modules, authors and original notes. Compilation repair: diagonalModuleSheafAbelian and diagonalAbSheafAbelian name the actual existing Mathlib abelian structures once, via inferInstance, sharing their sheafification witnesses throughout subsequent types. They contain real data, introduce no alternative category or additional hypotheses, and leave every original declaration and all six sorry proofs unchanged. This avoids repeated nested-proof abstraction and expensive kernel comparison of freshly synthesized abelian structures.
